knowledge:
- key_parameters: line=logical indicating whether to draw the sequence line in plotHelix, plotDoubleHelix, and plotOverlapHelix ;; arrow=logical indicating whether to draw direction arrows on the arcs ;; scale=logical indicating whether to scale the plot in plotOverlapHelix ;; log=logical indicating whether to log-transform values for coloring in colourByValue ;; get=logical indicating whether to return the colored structure/colors in coloring functions ;; palette=vector of custom colors for alignment or arc visualization ;; conflict.col=color assigned to conflicting basepairs (arcs sharing a base) in plotCovariance ;; base.colour=logical indicating whether to color bases in plotCovariance ;; species=index or identifier for the species/sequence to display in alignment plots ;; grid=logical indicating whether to draw a grid in alignment plots ;; text=logical indicating whether to display sequence text in alignment plots
- alternatives: None mentioned in the documentation, though standard RNA visualization tools exist. R is preferred here for its native support for publication-quality graphics and interactive power with large datasets.
- when_to_use: Use this package when you need to compare predicted RNA secondary structures (e.g., from TRANSAT) against known structures (e.g., from RFAM), or when you want to visualize multiple sequence alignments alongside secondary structure annotations to analyze covariation, conservation, and canonical base-pairing.
- pitfalls: Structures with conflicting basepairs (arcs sharing a base) cannot be visualized properly on a multiple sequence alignment and typically need to be filtered out or colored specifically (e.g., using conflict.col). Working with helices of length greater than 1 can limit flexibility; it is often necessary to break them into basepairs of length 1 using expandHelix before advanced coloring or filtering.

workflows.name: comparative_structure_visualization
workflows.intent: Compare predicted and known RNA secondary structures using single, double, and overlapping arc diagrams, including filtering and coloring by p-values.
input: predicted_structure.txt (predicted RNA structure in helix format)
known_structure.dbn (known RNA structure in dot-bracket/Vienna format)
workflows.stages: 1. Read predicted structure using readHelix and known structure using readVienna. ;; 2. Expand helices to basepairs of length 1 using expandHelix. ;; 3. Plot single structure using plotHelix. ;; 4. Plot double structure using plotDoubleHelix. ;; 5. Filter predicted structure by value (e.g., p-value). ;; 6. Color predicted structure by value using colourByValue and plot double helix with legend. ;; 7. Plot overlapping structures using plotOverlapHelix.
workflows.code:
library(R4RNA)

message("TRANSAT prediction in helix format")
transat_file <- system.file("extdata", "helix.txt", package = "R4RNA")
transat <- readHelix(transat_file)

message("RFAM structure in dot bracket format")
known_file <- system.file("extdata", "vienna.txt", package = "R4RNA")
known <- readVienna(known_file)

message("Work with basepairs instead of helices for more flexibility")
message("Breaks all helices into helices of length 1")
transat <- expandHelix(transat)
known <- expandHelix(known)

plotHelix(known, line = TRUE, arrow = TRUE)
mtext("Known Structure", side = 3, line = -2, adj = 0)

plotDoubleHelix(transat, known, line = TRUE, arrow = TRUE)
mtext("TRANSAT\nPredicted\nStructure", side = 3, line = -5, adj = 0)
mtext("Known Structure", side = 1, line = -2, adj = 0)

message("Filter out helices above a certain p-value")
transat <- transat[which(transat$value <= 1e-3), ]

message("Assign colour to basepairs according to p-value")
transat$col <- col <- colourByValue(transat, log = TRUE)

message("Coloured encoded in 'col' column of transat structure")
plotDoubleHelix(transat, known, line = TRUE, arrow = TRUE)

legend("topright", legend = attr(col, "legend"), fill = attr(col, "fill"),
    inset = 0.05, bty = "n", border = NA, cex = 0.75, title = "TRANSAT P-values")

plotOverlapHelix(transat, known, line = TRUE, arrow = TRUE, scale = FALSE)

workflows.name: alignment_and_structural_covariance
workflows.intent: Visualize RNA secondary structure on top of a multiple sequence alignment, annotating alignment and arcs by covariation, conservation, canonical base-pairing, or pseudoknots.
input: alignment.fasta (multiple sequence alignment in FASTA format)
known_structure.dbn (known RNA structure in dot-bracket/Vienna format)
workflows.stages: 1. Read alignment using readBStringSet and convert to character. ;; 2. Plot covariance of alignment with known structure using plotCovariance. ;; 3. Plot covariance with predicted structure, handling conflicting basepairs with conflict.col. ;; 4. Color and plot by covariation using colourByCovariation and plotCovariance. ;; 5. Color and plot by conservation using colourByConservation and plotCovariance. ;; 6. Color and plot by percentage canonical basepairs using colourByCanonical and plotCovariance. ;; 7. Color and plot pseudoknots using colourByUnknottedGroups and plotCovariance.
workflows.code:
library(R4RNA)
library(Biostrings)

transat_file <- system.file("extdata", "helix.txt", package = "R4RNA")
transat <- readHelix(transat_file)
known_file <- system.file("extdata", "vienna.txt", package = "R4RNA")
known <- readVienna(known_file)
transat <- expandHelix(transat)
known <- expandHelix(known)

message("Multiple sequence alignment of interest")
fasta_file <- system.file("extdata", "fasta.txt", package = "R4RNA")
fasta <- as.character(readBStringSet(fasta_file))

message("Plot covariance in alignment")
plotCovariance(fasta, known, cex = 0.5)

plotCovariance(fasta, transat, cex = 0.5, conflict.col = "grey")

col <- colourByCovariation(known, fasta, get = TRUE)
plotCovariance(fasta, col, grid = TRUE, legend = FALSE)
legend("topright", legend = attr(col, "legend"), fill = attr(col, "fill"),
    inset = 0.1, bty = "n", border = NA, cex = 0.37, title = "Covariation")

custom_colours <- c("green", "blue", "cyan", "red", "black", "grey")
plotCovariance(fasta, col <- colourByConservation(known, fasta, get = TRUE),
    palette = custom_colours, cex = 0.5)
legend("topright", legend = attr(col, "legend"), fill = attr(col, "fill"),
    inset = 0.15, bty = "n", border = NA, cex = 0.75, title = "Conservation")

col <- colourByCanonical(known, fasta, custom_colours, get = TRUE)
plotCovariance(fasta, col, base.colour = TRUE, cex = 0.5)
legend("topright", legend = attr(col, "legend"), fill = attr(col, "fill"),
    inset = 0.15, bty = "n", border = NA, cex = 0.75, title = "% Canonical")

col <- colourByUnknottedGroups(known, c("red", "blue"), get = TRUE)
plotCovariance(fasta, col, base.colour = TRUE, legend = FALSE, species = 23, grid = TRUE, text = TRUE, text.cex = 0.2, cex = 0.5)
